speaker: Doctor
text: Please describe your current symptoms in detail, specifically regarding any issues with walking, balance, or coordination. Additionally, what other medical conditions or history have you been diagnosed with previously?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: How long has this gait disturbance and clumsiness been progressing, and have you noticed any changes in your vision or speech? Also, have you ever been diagnosed with a condition like Multiple Sclerosis or syphilis?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy. REQUEST IMAGES: MRI_Brain_with_contrast.

The combination of gait ataxia, limb incoordination, and your history of Crohn's disease treated with natalizumab strongly suggests PML, a rare brain infection associated with this medication. An MRI of your brain is the critical next step to confirm this diagnosis.
